value.body: A sports physiotherapist works with athletes to prevent injuries, treat them when they happen and guide the return to play. Employers include sports teams, academies, fitness centres, sports-medicine clinics and sports bodies. Days mix injury screening and taping at training with treatment sessions, rehab plans and match-day cover.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BPT, often followed by an MPT (Sports)

items.label: Work settings
items.value: Teams, academies, gyms and sports-medicine clinics

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Taping, exercise equipment, strength and movement testing

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Finish a BPT and internship, then build sports exposure; volunteering at tournaments, academies or clubs is a common start. Many add an MPT (Sports) or sports-physiotherapy certifications before getting team roles.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Injury assessment on the field and in the clinic
Working alongside coaches, trainers and doctors

value.title: At a glance
items: Team roles are few and competitive; many work in clinics or gyms alongside event work.
Work follows the sports calendar, with travel and weekend matches.
Later roles include lead physiotherapist for a team or academy, or running a sports-injury clinic.
